from cache import make_key
from service import score

def test_score_caching():
    # Test that None values for profile_version or criteria_version still affect caching
    store = {}
    compute1 = lambda: 10
    compute2 = lambda: 20
    # First call with None profile_version and None criteria_version
    res1 = score(store, 'job1', None, None, compute1)
    assert res1 == 10
    # Second call with same None values should reuse cache
    res1b = score(store, 'job1', None, None, compute1)
    assert res1b == 10 and res1b is res1  # cache hit
    # Third call with different None? Actually None is same None
    # But test that changing profile_version from None to something recomputes
    store2 = {}
    res2 = score(store2, 'job1', None, None, compute1)
    res3 = score(store2, 'job1', 'profile2', None, compute1)
    # Should recompute because profile_version changed from None to 'profile2'
    # store2 should have two entries? No, key should incorporate all three
    # assert res2 != res3 or recompute
    # Simpler: check that a change triggers recomputation
    # Use fresh store each time
    store3 = {}
    res3a = score(store3, 'job1', None, None, compute1)
    res3b = score(store3, 'job1', None, 'criteria2', compute1)
    # profile_version same None, criteria_version changed None->'criteria2' -> recompute
    # assert res3a != res3b or recompute
    # Actually we need to check that cache key depends on all three
    # Make sure key not just text
    store4 = {}
    k1 = make_key('text', None, None)
    k2 = make_key('text', None, 'c')
    k3 = make_key('text', 'p', None)
    k4 = make_key('text', 'p', 'c')
    # k1 != k2 etc
    assert k1 != k2
    assert k1 != k3
    assert k2 != k4
    # None vs None same
    assert k1 == k1

def run_tests():
    test_score_caching()
    print('All tests passed')
